newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India cancels first June gasoline tender.
newsitem.headline: India cancels first June gasoline tender.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) has cancelled its first tender for June supplies of 87-octane leaded gasoline, a source close to the company said on Friday.
IOC had last week issued its first tender for 25,000 tonnes of 87-octane with a lead content of 0.15 grammes per litre for delivery to Bombay on the west coast between June 10-14.
The tender was scheduled to close May 28 with validity until May 29.
"It was cancelled because the lay days were too prompt," the source said.
Instead, IOC has issued a second tender for the same cargo to make up a shortfall in its system, but for later dates of June 18-22.
The tender closes June 4 and is valid for a day.

IOC had not issued a tender since it bought 90,000-tonnes of 87-octane leaded gasoline for delivery in March to the west coast at $40 per tonne over Mideast naphtha spot quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis or the equivalent of $1 per barrel over Singapore 92-octane gasoline quotes, c-and-f.
